findings.verdictNotes:
The claim is partially confirmed with important caveats and corrections:

CONFIRMED ASPECTS:
1. Opacity threshold gradients DO exist (0.08–0.30) as stated:
   - near_invisible_opacity: 0.08–0.15 (line 168-176, scoring.ts)
   - low_opacity: 0.15–0.30 (line 177-184, scoring.ts)
   - invisible_but_clickable: <0.08 (line 164-167, scoring.ts)
   - cursor_pointer_no_affordance also uses <0.3 threshold (line 188)

2. Tests verify boundaries (e.g., lines 263-277 in scoring.test.ts verify near_invisible_opacity and low_opacity fire at 0.10 and 0.20)

REFUTED/CORRECTED ASPECTS:
1. "No calibration comment" — REFUTED: The code has explicit inline comments explaining the gradient logic (lines 169-170, 178, showing values and interpolation)

2. "Tests verify boundaries but don't validate FP on real benign sites" — REFUTED: The FP measurement DID happen. The roadmap states "False positive measurement on Tranco top-1000" is a Phase 1 gate (line 340+), and actual FP measurement run produced results (tranco-measurement-2026-05-01.md with 0.72% FP rate on Tranco top-200)

3. "Tranco FP measurement does not isolate opacity-based FPs" — PARTIALLY TRUE but mischaracterizes risk: While the FP report doesn't separately break down which reason codes caused FPs, the measured FP rate is 0.72% (~1 FP site), indicating opacity thresholds are NOT causing widespread false positives on benign sites.

4. "Lack of measured FP data" — REFUTED: FP data exists (fp-top50-20260425.csv, tranco-measurement-2026-05-01.md). The unity3d.com FP event had NRS 70 and 115; neither score appears to be explained primarily by low-opacity gradient alone—CDS smart-mode gating (line 1679, capture_isolated.ts) shows opacity-based reason codes are in RISKY_BLANK_REASONS (lines 90-91), meaning they prevent Smart Mode allowances.

5. Opacity values ARE captured in ElementHint and DOM builder (dom_builder.ts lines 70, 76), BUT the event_log extras field is currently unused (storage.ts lines 298 shows extra support exists but callers don't populate it with opacity data). This is a valid observation that logging could be richer.

6. No 'legitimate_transparency' corpus label exists—TRUE, but the gym contains opacity evasion fixtures (evasion-01-opacity-009.html, evasion-09-filter-opacity.html) used in testing.

SEVERITY ASSESSMENT: Severity rated "high" appears overstated. The actual state:
- Gradient scoring works and is tested
- Real-world FP measurement was performed (0.72% on Tranco top-200)
- No evidence of opacity gradients causing endemic false positives
- Smart Mode already gates on opacity-related reason codes to reduce false positives

The valid gap: Opacity values are not logged in event_log extras when near_invisible_opacity/low_opacity fires, limiting post-hoc analysis. This is a data-collection gap, not a detection gap.

findings.verdictNotes:

findings.title: intent_mismatch_under_interactive (+35) drives unity3d.com FP (0.72% Tranco rate)
findings.evidence: extension/src/shared/scoring.ts lines 128–137. This is a genuine FP affecting real users navigating between unity.com and unity3d.com.
findings.recommendation: Log intent_mismatch_under_interactive with DOM context (top element tag/role, underlying tag/role, semantic relationship hints). Implement heuristic: if top element is container-like (nav, div role=navigation) without action intent, don't flag. Test on corpus with intentional nested interactivity.
findings.verdictNotes:
CONFIRMED. Code evidence directly supports the claim:

1. **Signal verification**: extension/src/shared/scoring.ts lines 128-137 implements intent_mismatch_under_interactive with +35 CDS score. Condition: underlying element is interactive with name, top is NOT (interactive AND named).

2. **Tranco FP evidence**: tests/fp-results/tranco-measurement-2026-05-01.md lines 115-149 confirms unity3d.com FP: NRS=70 from intent_mismatch (+35) + nrs_cross_site (+20) + nrs_fast_attempt (+10) + nrs_user_activation_active (+5) = exactly at NRS_BLOCK_THRESHOLD. Measurement confirms 0.72% FP rate (1/138 successful visits).

3. **No container heuristic gating**: extension/src/shared/scoring.ts lines 65-72 show isInteractive() only checks tag (A/BUTTON), role (link/button), hasOnClick. No filtering for nav/container roles or "without action intent" logic exists. The recommendation in measurement doc lines 139-145 to "if top element is container-like (nav, div role=navigation) without action intent, don't flag" is NOT implemented.

4. **No Smart Mode filtering**: Verified capture_isolated.ts getNrsBlockThreshold() and scoring path - no conditional filtering of intent_mismatch in any mode.

5. **Real user impact**: Measurement confirms genuine FP on legitimate unity.com cross-domain links to other Unity-owned domains, NOT a measurement artifact.

Severity (0.72% FP rate on Tranco top-200) is above 0.1% target and represents a well-understood composite scoring issue waiting for implementation of recommended container-aware heuristics.

findings.title: No rich context telemetry; corpus missing raw inputs for tuning (critical for goal 3)
findings.evidence: extension/src/shared/storage.ts lines 55–64: PromptOutcomeEntry stores only (id, ts, domain, destDomain, type, score, outcome, reasons). No ClickContext (opacity, coverage_ratio, z-index, accessibility name) is appended when user responds to prompt. extension/src/content/capture_isolated.ts stores lastDebug with full context but this is never appended to outcome entry.
findings.recommendation: Extend PromptOutcomeEntry to include optional 'context' field with serialized ClickContext and nrs/cds breakdown. When prompt outcome is recorded, append lastDebug state. This enables post-hoc analysis: 'show all FPs where opacity was 0.12–0.18' and measure TP rate, adjust weight.
findings.verdictNotes:
CONFIRMED: The claim is accurate. When users respond to prompts in Smart Mode, the rich click context is NOT appended to PromptOutcomeEntry.

Evidence from code:

1. PromptOutcomeEntry interface (extension/src/shared/storage.ts:55-64) contains only: id, ts, domain, destDomain?, type, score, outcome, reasons? — NO context field.

2. All prompt outcome recordings in capture_isolated.ts skip the context:
   - Line 1325-1330: "Allow once" button calls appendPromptOutcome() with only {domain, destDomain, type, score, outcome}
   - Line 1345-1351: "Always allow" button uses appendOutcomeSafely() with same limited fields
   - Line 1373-1379: Dismiss handler uses appendOutcomeSafely() with same fields
   - Line 1724-1729: Block outcome also only records {domain, type, score, outcome}

3. Credential prompts (credential_guard.ts:188-213) follow the same pattern — no context appended.

4. Meanwhile, lastDebug (line 1756 in capture_isolated.ts) DOES store the full ClickContext with all required fields:
   - opacity (from ElementHint.opacity via ctx.top/underlying)
   - z-index (from ElementHint.zIndex)
   - coverage_ratio (computable from rect + viewport dimensions)
   - accessibility name data (ariaLabelLength, titleLength, textLength from ElementHint)

5. Prompts DO occur in Smart Mode: Line 1681 shows prompts trigger when mode !== "off" (includes smart), lines 1684-1688 show decision="prompt" logic executes in Smart Mode.

6. The context is never appended: appendPromptOutcome() receives a partial parameter type that excludes context fields. No post-hoc injection of context happens either in appendPromptOutcome, appendPromptOutcomeDirect, or persistPromptOutcome functions.

The severity assessment as "critical for goal 3" appears accurate if goal 3 involves post-hoc analysis like "show all FPs where opacity was 0.12–0.18" — that data cannot be recovered from the stored outcomes.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE: No offline corpus export; telemetry trapped in-extension, blocking tuning feedback loops
findings.evidence: Goal 3 requires 'local labeled corpus to drive tuning.' EventLogEntry and PromptOutcomeEntry are stored in chrome.storage.local with no export mechanism. corpus-validation test manually extracts via service-worker.evaluate(), but no UI/API for users to export logs offline. Researchers/tuning loops cannot access real-world patterns without manual intervention.
findings.recommendation: Add export function to service worker serializing event_log + prompt_outcomes + domain_profile in JSON format. Add UI menu 'Export diagnosis log'. This enables: (1) user bug reports with full context, (2) offline analysis on opt-in logs, (3) feedback loops for adaptive scoring. Privacy: local-only, user-initiated.
findings.verdictNotes:
CORE ISSUE CONFIRMED but details and severity are MISREPRESENTED:

CONFIRMED: (1) EventLogEntry and PromptOutcomeEntry lack rich feature vectors (missing full CDS/NRS breakdown, redirect chains, gesture timing, DOM hints). (2) These are stored in chrome.storage.local with size limits (eventLog max 5000 entries per getEventLog:281, promptOutcomes max 500 entries per PROMPT_OUTCOMES_LIMIT:322). (3) The telemetry is outcome-only, not replay-grade, matching the NORTHSTAR_RESEARCH_HANDOFF.md Goal 3 gap analysis (line 162-164).

REFUTED: (1) "No export mechanism" — exportAll() function exists and is accessible via an "Export" button in options.html:31, downloadable as JSON (storage.ts:732-756, options.ts:540-552). (2) "Manually extracts via service-worker.evaluate()" being the ONLY way — users can export via the UI. The test corpus-validation.spec.ts:132-146 uses sw.evaluate() only for automated testing, not because it's the only export path. (3) "Blocked tuning feedback loops" — the export is NOT blocked; users can immediately export for offline analysis. The issue is that the exported schema lacks the detailed feature breakdown needed for retraining (the real gap).

MISALIGNED: The recommendation says "export... domain_profile" but exportAll() does NOT include domain_profile; it includes adaptiveScores instead (storage.ts:739). The claim calls it "Export diagnosis log" but the actual UI labels it "Export" and exports the full suite state, not a scoped diagnosis.

SEVERITY DOWNGRADE: The gap is real (schema incomplete for offline retraining) but NOT a blocker to "user bug reports with full context" or "offline analysis." The export already enables (1) and partially (2). The actual gap is (3) offline feedback-loop retraining — needs richer schemas (per-decision feature breakdown, redirect chain, DOM hints), not just an export mechanism.

- options.ts:540-552 (Export button handler)
- options.html:31 (Export button in UI)
- storage.ts:261-271 (EventLogEntry)

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE: Content script cannot inspect cross-origin iframes; XSS on subframes undetected
findings.evidence: Goal 4 (ARCHITECTURE LEVERAGE). Extension operates at main-world/isolated-world on top frame only (extension/src/content/dom_builder.ts, capture_isolated.ts). Subframes (iframes, shadow DOM, portals) not fully inspected or only after payload executes. Attacker loads malicious iframe.com inside bank.com—click in iframe bypasses all detection. Chrome MV3 limits subframe access.
findings.recommendation: Architect native-messaging companion app (Phase V0) that receives click + navigation telemetry from extension. App maintains persistent threat model (known-bad subframe origins, cross-origin frame relationships) and validates clicks across frame boundaries. Enables offline corpus collection and ML-based tuning. Keep bridge minimal (click events, frame relationships).
findings.verdictNotes:
The core architectural issue is real but with important clarifications:

CONFIRMED:
- Content scripts run in cross-origin iframes (manifest.json all_frames: true, line 36, 43)
- DOM inspection (elementsFromPoint, composedPath) is frame-scoped and cannot see parent frame's DOM (dom_builder.ts:127, 145)
- Overlay detection fails when click occurs in iframe with parent-frame overlay (capture_isolated.ts:1535 uses frame-scoped context only)
- No special frame-gating in Smart Mode block decision (line 1681-1684 applies identically to top frame and subframes)
- In child frames, bloom filter reputation check skipped, only async post-decision check (line 1600-1608, 1788-1813)

SCENARIO VALIDITY:
The specific attack (bank.com overlay + evil.com iframe click) bypasses detection because:
- CDS computed from iframe's DOM elements (low/zero)
- NRS = low CDS + factors (~20-30 vs threshold 70 in Smart Mode)
- Blocking fails; async reputation check is too late

MITIGATIONS/DETAILS NOT FULLY MATCHING CLAIM:
- "Payload executes" is imprecise - clicks in iframes ARE detected, but scoring is broken
- Reputation check exists but is async/non-blocking (line 1788+)
- Not a complete architectural "blind spot" - more a detection evasion via frame boundary opacity
- Description mentions "main-world/isolated-world on top frame only" but code shows both run in all_frames

VERDICT: Architectural gap confirmed (iframe overlay detection failure), but implementation details differ from claim's framing.

findings.title: isLegitModalBackdrop limited to role='dialog'/aria-modal; CSS-only modals undetected
findings.evidence: extension/src/content/dom_builder.ts (inferred): detectLegitModalBackdrop checks ancestor for role='dialog' or aria-modal='true'. Many legitimate modals lack these attributes (older libraries, custom implementations, jQuery plugins). Leads to FPs on CSS-only modals.
findings.recommendation: Extend detectLegitModalBackdrop to recognize CSS patterns (class names 'modal', 'dialog', 'overlay') and fixed/absolute backdrop with z-index ≥999 and opacity 0.3–0.8. Test on corpus with CSS modals (Bootstrap, Material-UI).
findings.verdictNotes: The claim is confirmed. The `detectLegitModalBackdrop` function in extension/src/content/dom_builder.ts (lines 104-122) ONLY checks for role='dialog' or aria-modal='true' and does NOT check for CSS-based modal patterns (class names like 'modal', 'dialog', 'overlay'). This limitation applies in both Smart and Strict modes - there is no mode-specific gating that would address this. The function is called during click detection (line 168) and reduces CDS by 20 points when a legitimate modal is detected (scoring.ts:199-202). CSS-only modals from Bootstrap, Material-UI, jQuery plugins, or custom implementations lacking these ARIA attributes will not be detected, leading to false positives. The codebase contains CSS pattern detection in mutation_monitor.ts for cookie banners/chat widgets (lines 85-110), but this is separate infrastructure not integrated into the click-time modal backdrop detection. The recommendation to extend detectLegitModalBackdrop with CSS patterns is valid and currently unimplemented.

findings.title: Adaptive scoring threshold adjustment is sound but never applied to decision thresholds
findings.evidence: extension/src/shared/adaptive_scoring.ts lines 25–93: computeAdjustment() is principled and defensive. But extension/src/content/capture_isolated.ts computes adaptiveAdj without applying it—decision threshold remains hard-coded as NRS_BLOCK_THRESHOLD (70). Adjustment is logged (lastDebug.adaptiveAdj) but dormant.
findings.recommendation: Integrate adaptive adjustment: decision_threshold = BASE_THRESHOLD + adaptiveAdj. This reduces FPs on trusted domains (auto-allow more) and increases blocks on attack-history domains. Add UI label showing 'Threshold: 70 → 75 (trusted)' for explainability.

findings.title: Composite escalation (+10/+15 at 3+/4+ factors) can over-weight benign combinations
findings.evidence: extension/src/shared/scoring.ts lines 204–210: if 3+ non-mitigating reason codes fire, +10; if 4+, +15. Example: carousel with (1) no_accessible_name, (2) retargeted_target_mismatch, (3) overlay_medium_interactive hits 3 factors and auto-escalates. No corpus data isolates 'composite_escalation' FPs.
findings.recommendation: Add composite_escalation to event_log extras (with list of stacked factors). Measure FP rate separately. If >1%, implement weighted composite model (escalate if sum of factor weights exceeds threshold, not just count).

findings.title: z-index gradient floor (5000) and scaling formula lack evidence
findings.evidence: extension/src/shared/scoring.ts lines 145–157: formula yields 1 point at z=5001, 10 at z=9999. Tests verify boundaries but no FP measurement on legitimate high z-index (autofill dropdowns at z=2147483647, tooltips at z=99999). 5000 threshold appears arbitrary.
findings.recommendation: Audit z-index on Tranco corpus; find distribution. Measure FP rate for z-index-only signals separately. Consider adjusting floor to 2000 or requiring z-index to fire only with visibility/opacity anomaly.

findings.title: NAV_ANOMALY burst detection not calibrated against benign bursts (SPA nav, multi-tab workflows)
findings.evidence: extension/src/shared/nav_anomaly.ts lines 482–527: anomaly fires if category <5% total AND 2+ navs in 30s. No corpus data on legitimate benign bursts (rapid shopping, multi-tab reading, OAuth chains).
findings.recommendation: Log nav_anomaly fires with (source_category, destination_category, burst_count, total_navigations). Run corpus on workflows known to trigger bursts. Refine categories to separate high-risk (walletconnect.com, binance.com) from low-risk (coinmarketcap.com) within crypto.

findings.title: ClickFix score (0–60 capped at 40) not calibrated against real CAPTCHA pages
findings.evidence: extension/src/shared/nrs.ts lines 166–169: clickfixScore capped at 40. Scanner (extension/src/content/clickfix_detector.ts) detects 2+ of 3 signals (clipboard write, overlay, CAPTCHA text) but thresholds appear hand-tuned. No test on legitimate copy-to-clipboard + modal combos.
findings.recommendation: Log clickfix scan results (signals fired, score, decision) in event_log extras. Run corpus on legitimate copy UI (GitHub, Stack Overflow). If FP >0.5%, implement heuristic to suppress ClickFix on domains with legitimate copy UI.

findings.title: JS behavior scoring lacks FP measurement on benign dynamic forms
findings.evidence: extension/src/shared/js_behavior_state.ts lines 32–37: SCORE_CROSS_ORIGIN_CREDENTIAL_FORM (15), SCORE_DYNAMIC_FORM_ACTION (10), etc., capped per-signal. No test on benign dynamic forms (form.action set by JS routing, credential read for validation, AJAX submit). No veto list for legitimate libraries.
