findings.title: Gym Fixture Benchmark Baseline Created But 'lastRun' is Null — No Historical Trend Tracking of Category TP/FP Rates
findings.evidence: scripts/benchmark.mjs (lines 61-150) defines CORPUS with 49 fixtures across 7 categories. Lines 818-833 create benchmark JSON with thresholds (clickjacking: minTpRate 80%, maxFpRate 10%, etc.) and store in scripts/benchmark-baseline.json. Current baseline (via cat command output): thresholds populated, 'lastRun: null' — no actual run data. Lines 796-797 show analysis object has categories{} but no prior runs are stored. Result: (1) CI can compare this run to baseline thresholds but not to previous runs (no delta detection), (2) slow regressions undetectable (e.g., TP rate drifting from 92% → 85% → 80% would not trigger alarm until it crosses 80% threshold), (3) markdown summary (lines 589-684) compares to baseline but only regressions section shows deviations.
findings.recommendation: Modify benchmark.mjs to: (1) Store an array of timestamped runs in benchmarks.json: { runs: [{timestamp, categories{}, overall{}}], thresholds{} }, keep last 20 runs. (2) In CI, compute trend for each category (TP rate over last 3 runs) and warn if downward trend > 2pp/run. (3) Report in markdown: 'TP Rate for Clickjacking: 92% (↓ from 93%, 94% last two runs)'. (4) Export a simple CSV of TP/FP over time for dashboard/graphing.
findings.verdictNotes: Core claim is accurate: benchmark.mjs (line 830) stores only a single `lastRun` in the baseline, enabling comparison to one previous run but NOT multi-run trend tracking. However, key discrepancy: claim states "49 fixtures across 7 categories" but CORPUS actually contains 53 fixtures (lines 61-150). The baseline-baseline.json confirms lastRun is currently null (line 33). The code (line 558: `baseline.lastRun?.categories ?? {}`) can compare to previous run data IF lastRun is populated, so it's not completely without history. However, the critical gap is accurate: there is NO array of timestamped runs (no `runs: [{timestamp, categories{}}]` structure), only a single lastRun property. This prevents true trend detection across 3+ runs and gradual regression detection—confirmed by absence of historical array logic in compareBaseline (lines 524-585) and markdown generation (lines 627-634 improvements section only compares current vs one previous, with no downward-trend-per-run calculation). The markdown reporting (lines 589-684) correctly shows regressions vs thresholds and improvements vs lastRun, but cannot report "TP Rate drifting 92% → 85% → 80%%" as the recommendation suggests because only lastRun exists, not a run history.

findings.title: Smart Mode Silence Goal (Zero False Positives on Benign Browsing) Has No Dedicated CI Gate Beyond Generic FP Measurement
findings.evidence: PRODUCT VISION goal #1 (from task description): 'ZERO false positives in everyday Smart Mode browsing — extension must be silent during normal use (SSO logins, OAuth flows, payment popups, SPAs, redirect-heavy marketing links, cloud-hosted apps)'. measure-fp.mjs visits homepage + 3 internal links (~30-60 seconds per site). Does NOT test: (1) multi-step login with credential entry and form submission (credential-guard tests exist separately in tests/e2e/credential-guard.spec.ts lines but not in FP harness), (2) OAuth redirect chains (only top-level nav tested, not full auth flow), (3) payment checkout flows, (4) SPA route changes with complex state. No CI gate explicitly named 'Smart Mode Silence' or 'Silent Browsing' — closest is the generic 0.1% FP threshold which lumps together nav FPs, cred FPs, and interaction FPs. Project Roadmap.md line 60 lists 'D19: FP measurement is a Phase 1 gate' but no code implementing this gate in .github/workflows/.
findings.recommendation: Create a dedicated 'Smart Mode Silence CI Gate' that separately measures: (1) Nav-only FP rate (current measure-fp.mjs, target <0.1%), (2) Credential-flow FP rate (visit pages with password forms, attempt form submission, target 0% on legitimate pages). (3) Document in PR template that scoring changes require both gates to pass. (4) If either gate regresses, CI fails. This directly validates PRODUCT VISION goal #1. Track separately in benchmarks.json: { nav_fps: 0.42%, cred_fps: 0.0% } so you know which dimension is at risk.
findings.verdictNotes: The core claim is confirmed: NavSentinel has a stated goal of "Zero false positives in everyday Smart Mode browsing" (documented in NORTHSTAR_RESEARCH_HANDOFF.md as "Goal 1 — Zero-FP Smart Mode"), but this goal has NO dedicated CI gate. Evidence: (1) measure-fp.mjs (lines 1-21, 450-485) tests only homepage + 3 link clicks + scrolling, NOT credential submission flows, OAuth chains, payment flows, or complex SPA navigation. (2) FP_EVENT_KINDS (lines 41-47) includes cred_* events but only triggers if user manually submits forms, which measure-fp.mjs never does. (3) .github/workflows/ci.yml (lines 62-95) runs "npm run test:e2e" on playwright smoke/regression tests, NOT "npm run measure-fp". measure-fp is a manual command (not in CI). (4) benchmark-baseline.json shows per-category TP/FP thresholds, NOT the split "nav_fps" + "cred_fps" tracking recommended. (5) Project Roadmap.md line 751 explicitly states Phase 2 gate item as "[ ] No regression in Phase 1 measurements (FP rate, TP rate) — needs re-run after P4 additions (blocked on FP re-measurement run)" - meaning FP measurement is not a blocking CI gate, only a manual gate. The severity is accurate (critical for a UX-gap) because the product vision explicitly targets zero false positives but relies on manual testing that only covers navigation interactions, not the full user flow (login, OAuth, payments, complex SPAs) that the goal claims to protect.

findings.title: Event Log + Explanation Infrastructure Exists But User-Facing Decision Journal Missing — FRIEND-ADVISOR UX Goal Unmeasured
findings.evidence: extension/src/shared/storage.ts (lines 261-271): EventLogEntry schema with score, reasons[], extra{}. tests/explanations.test.ts verifies all 30+ reason codes map to <80-char explanations. extension/src/shared/explanations.ts lines 1-69: code mapping complete (e.g., 'no_accessible_name' → 'This clickable area has no visible label'). PRODUCT VISION goal #2: 'FRIEND-ADVISOR UX — every decision the extension makes (block, prompt, silent score, suppressed signal) should be explainable to the user in plain language via a verbose mode / decision journal'. Current state: reasons stored in event log, explanations defined in code, but UI does not expose reasoning path. No test of whether user understands the explanation or finds it helpful. demo-showcase tests (tests/e2e/demo-showcase.*.spec.ts) are scripted walkthroughs, not user feedback loops.
findings.recommendation: Implement a 'Verbose Decision Journal' in options page that displays (for recent prompts): (1) timeline with date, domain, event type, (2) score breakdown: CDS score [factors], NRS score [factors], composite, (3) threshold applied, (4) plain-language explanation from explainReasonCode(). Make this exportable (JSON/CSV). Add a feedback mechanism: 'Was this explanation clear? [Yes] [No] [Not sure]' logged to event_log.extra.feedbackClear=true/false. Set a goal: > 80% of users say 'yes'. This directly validates PRODUCT VISION goal #2 and creates a feedback loop for tuning explanation wording.
findings.verdictNotes: Core claim is confirmed: Event log infrastructure exists with score/reasons/extra fields (storage.ts:261-271), explanations are defined and mapped (explanations.ts:1-69, ~49 codes not 30+), and tests verify coverage (explanations.test.ts:1-145). However, the infrastructure is incomplete on the user-facing side: (1) explanations.ts exists and all 49 reason codes map to <80-char plain-English text, (2) BUT explainReasonCode is used ONLY in capture_isolated.ts:105 for toast messages, never in the UI. (3) The options page event log (options.ts:285-327) displays raw reason code names, NOT the explanations—renderEventLog shows event.reasons as plain code strings, not translated via explainReasonCode(). (4) No verbose mode, decision journal UI, feedback mechanism ("Was this clear?"), or user-facing explanation rendering exists anywhere in extension/src/. (5) The NORTHSTAR_RESEARCH_HANDOFF.md (lines 14-15, 24) documents FRIEND-ADVISOR UX as an explicit goal: "every decision (block, prompt, silent score, suppressed signal) explainable in plain language via verbose mode / a decision journal." The gap is real and documented: §4 (Goal 2) states "there is no *user-facing* decision journal—a reviewable timeline of what did NavSentinel decide, when, and why, including silent decisions (suppressed signals, scores below threshold)." The building blocks (explanations.ts + event_log storage) exist but the user-facing layer to display them and measure user comprehension does not. Claim is confirmed as stated.

findings.title: MV3 Architectural Limits Known But Not Systematically Verified in Test Suite
findings.evidence: measure-fp.mjs (lines 319-326) comments on MV3 service worker recycling: 'ephemeral; this handles the case where the worker has been recycled during a long measurement run.' extension/src/shared/storage.ts (lines 301-316) has retry logic for event append (3 attempts), hinting at storage/sync issues. no systematic test of: (1) what happens if storage quota exceeded (300-event limit set at line 84, clamped at lines 104-105, but no test of behavior when full), (2) service worker recycling under concurrent tab load, (3) message passing latency (content script → SW → content), (4) state isolation guarantees between tabs. playwright.stress.config.ts exists but not in CI, so stress tests don't run routinely.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Architecture Verification' test suite (tests/architecture-verification.test.ts or e2e/mv3-limits.spec.ts): (1) measure event append latency under 5+ concurrent tabs, (2) force service worker recycling and verify event loss rate < 0.1%, (3) fill storage to quota and verify graceful fallback, (4) measure SW message roundtrip latency and alert if > 500ms. Run nightly. Document MV3 constraints in docs/Architecture_and_Data_Flow.md with known limits and fallback strategies. This prevents silent data loss or latency blowups in production.
findings.verdictNotes:
The core issue of missing MV3 architectural limit verification is real, but the details and severity require clarification:

CONFIRMED aspects:
- Service worker recycling acknowledged in code (measure-fp.mjs:319-325) with comment about ephemeral workers during long runs
- Storage append has retry logic (3 attempts) indicating known fragility (storage.ts:301-315)
- Event log soft limit is 300 by default (storage.ts:84), though configurable to 50-5000 range (storage.ts:104)
- Stress test suite exists (playwright.stress.config.ts) but runs nightly only, NOT in main CI pipeline (ci.yml lines 1-137 show no stress test invocation)
- No systematic test of storage quota exhaustion, worker recycling event-loss rate, or multi-tab concurrent event throughput
- No latency measurement tests

PARTIALLY CONFIRMED / INACCURATE aspects:
- The "300-event limit" is misleading: it is a configurable DEFAULT (range 50-5000), not a hard MV3 architectural quota. The claim conflates soft user-configurable settings with hard platform limits.
- Storage limit enforcement IS tested in detail (storage-property.test.ts:455-504 tests appendEvent never exceeds logLimit; storage-append.test.ts:111-142 tests enforced limits). What is NOT tested is behavior when actual MV3 storage quota (10MB) is exceeded.
- Concurrent tab testing PARTIALLY exists (RW-23 stress test verifies 2-tab popup isolation, but does NOT test 5+ concurrent tabs or measure event append latency under concurrent load)
- Message passing latency NOT measured

The claim identifies a real gap in architectural stress verification (worker recycling event loss, concurrent tab load, actual quota breach), but overstates the "300-event limit" as a hard quota (it is soft/user-configurable) and understates that event-log soft-limit enforcement IS tested—just not under MV3 architectural stress conditions (heavy load, worker recycling, quota exhaustion).

findings.title: Stress/Timing Tests Defined (RW-21–RW-25, 5 Edge-Case Scenarios) but Not Wired Into CI
findings.evidence: Project Roadmap.md (lines 139-149 P0-02, lines 155-167 P0-03): RW-21 (allow-once double-spend), RW-22 (rollback after worker restart), RW-23 (multi-tab prompts), RW-24 (idle-resume popup), RW-25 (rapid close/reopen). playwright.stress.config.ts (lines 1-19): defines stress test project with @stress grep tag. Status from roadmap: 'Stress lane runs locally, npm run test:e2e:stress works' but line 166 says 'Or create a separate stress.yml workflow' — implying not yet done. .github/workflows/ likely only has ci.yml (main) and does not include stress.yml. These tests validate MV3 service worker recycling and tab isolation — critical for reliability — but skip in CI so regressions undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add .github/workflows/stress.yml (triggered nightly or on-demand, not blocking). Run stress tests separately from regression suite. Do not block merges on stress failure (they're long-running and may be flaky), but track results and alert if multiple failures. Store results in benchmarks.json under 'stress_runs' key. Document known MV3 constraints (service worker ephemeral lifecycle, tab isolation via storage events) in docs/Architecture_and_Data_Flow.md.

findings.title: No Continuous Phishing Corpus Refresh — TP Measurement is Point-in-Time, Not Trendy

This means it will not run in CI by default.' fetch-phishing-corpus.mjs has 24-hour cache (line 162) and can run nightly, but no automated job configured. findings.title: Browser-Specific Behavior (Chrome-Only Today) Not Tested — Firefox Port (P4-03) Pending But No Cross-Browser CI Framework

(2) Design plugin architecture so measurement scripts can accept --browser chrome|firefox. (3) When FF port opens, add Firefox tests in parallel to Chrome tests (not blocking for now). This prevents surprises during P4-03 implementation.

findings.title: Insufficient suppression of cross-site _blank anchors for legitimate SSO/OAuth flows
findings.evidence: capture_isolated.ts:1683-1689: Decision path for _blank anchors shows NRS=40-45 for typical SSO login (nrs_new_tab_window +20, nrs_cross_site +20, nrs_user_activation +5) stays below Smart threshold (70) but isLegitBlankAnchor() at 1679 gates only on visibility/name, not session frequency. Domain_profile.ts only penalizes repeat offenders, never suppresses. No mechanism prevents prompting legitimate _blank anchors that become frequent after 3-5 clicks.
findings.recommendation: Implement session-aware _blank suppression: track per-domain click frequency in current browser session. If _blank anchor to domain D allowed >=2 times in last 10 minutes, suppress nrs_new_tab_window (+20) and nrs_cross_site (+20) on next click. Alternatively, use domain_profile's 24h history to suppress these factors when domain has >=5 visits.
findings.verdictNotes:
The code analysis confirms the core claim: there is NO session-aware suppression of _blank anchor factors, and legitimate cross-site OAuth/SSO clicks will be repeatedly prompted in Smart mode.

CONFIRMED FINDINGS:
- NRS weights are correct: nrs_new_tab_window=+20, nrs_cross_site=+20, nrs_user_activation=+5 (nrs.ts:51-54)
- Typical legitimate SSO login NRS ≈ 45 (below Smart threshold of 70)
- isLegitBlankAnchor() (lines 1160-1175) only checks: CDS<70, visibility, name, interactivity, retargeting, risky reason codes — NO session frequency check
- domain_profile.ts applies repeat-offender penalty (+10 NRS) only AFTER domain meets thresholds (avgNRS>30, triggerCount>3) — does not suppress _blank factors, only adds bonus
- No session-based cache or frequency tracking exists for _blank anchors in capture_isolated.ts

INCORRECT DETAIL:
- Severity claim needs nuancing: This is NOT causing false BLOCKS (NRS stays at ~45, below 70 block threshold), but rather repeated PROMPTS. Users see repeated "Suspicious new tab" prompts for legitimate OAuth flows when clicking 3-5 SSO links per session. This is poor UX and may cause users to disable protection, but not a security bypass. Actual severity is medium (UX friction) not high (security).

VERIFICATION:
- capture_isolated.ts:1683-1688: Decision logic confirms that if smartAllowsBlank=true, the NRS check is skipped and navigation is allowed. But smartAllowsBlank does not consider session frequency.
- No session-based tracking found in codebase for _blank click frequency
- Domain profile only uses 24h history, not session-scoped (domain_profile.ts:57-78 decay age is 30 days)

findings.title: No explicit false-positive safeguard for legitimate clipboard-copy buttons adjacent to overlays
findings.evidence: clickfix_detector.ts uses '2-of-3 signals' rule but suppression relies on known CAPTCHA whitelists. Real scenario: docs site with 'Copy code' button + cookie-consent modal triggers clipboard_write + overlay. While scan requires command-like content OR CAPTCHA text to score >=25, non-command writes paired with overlays can still accumulate if text patterns match.
findings.recommendation: Add DOM whitelist for legitimate clipboard+overlay pairs: suppress ClickFix scan if overlay has cookie-consent class patterns (contains 'cookie', 'consent', 'gdpr', 'banner', 'notice'). Low-cost pattern-match eliminating the most common benign FP.
findings.verdictNotes:
The claim correctly identifies that clickfix_detector.ts lacks an explicit cookie-consent DOM whitelist (unlike mutation_monitor.ts which has COOKIE_CONSENT_PATTERNS at lines 85-96). However, the code has a STRONGER implicit safeguard than claimed:

1. **Non-command clipboard write + overlay alone scores 0 points** (lines 417-423): A copy of code snippet next to a cookie banner will NOT trigger, contrary to the concern. The scoring requires BOTH overlay AND (command-like content OR CAPTCHA/instruction text patterns).

2. **Actual false-positive scenario is constrained**:
   - Requires non-command clipboard write + overlay + instruction text patterns (e.g., "paste into terminal")
   - Most cookie banners don't meet overlay detection thresholds (minCoverage=25%, minZIndex=100)
   - Instruction patterns are attack-specific, not found on normal docs pages

3. **Verification of "2-of-3 signals" claim**: Line 437-441 confirms this—detects only if signalCount >= 2 AND score >= 25. The gating is correct.

4. **Missing safeguard**: The code comment at line 412-415 acknowledges clipboard+overlay FP risk but the integration with known-benign patterns (like cookie-consent) is NOT implemented in clickfix_detector itself.

5. **Smart Mode confirmation**: ClickFix detection is active in both smart and strict modes (line 915: `settings.defaultMode !== "off"`).

The recommendation is valid but the actual false-positive risk is lower than stated because of stricter scoring requirements and overlay size/z-index filters. The code is more defensive than the claim suggests, but yes, explicit cookie-consent suppression would reduce theoretical edge-case FPs.

findings.title: Redirect chain depth scoring not aware of legitimate marketing/UTM redirect patterns
findings.evidence: nrs.ts:132-136: redirect chain adds +5/hop capped at 25. Gym fixture documents OAuth/UTM/login redirects as legitimate but server-side. Real scenario: email->Mailchimp tracker->landing (3-hop) detected at navigation time. Service worker tracks chains but does not distinguish legitimate marketing redirectors from malicious ones.
findings.recommendation: Expand known-redirector list to include legitimate marketing (Mailchimp, Google Analytics). Add source context: if referrer is corporate email domain and chain includes marketing redirector, suppress penalty. Or: if all hops stay within same registrable domain or related organization domains (domain_groups.ts), suppress chain depth penalty entirely.
findings.verdictNotes:
The claim correctly identifies that redirect chain depth scoring adds +5 points per hop over threshold 2, capped at 25 (nrs.ts:60-62, 132-137). Mailchimp and other legitimate marketing redirectors ARE in the TRACKING_PREFIX_ALLOWLIST (redirect_chain.ts:59-67) so they correctly return FALSE from isKnownRedirector(), preventing the +15 "known redirector" penalty.

However, the core issue is REAL but more subtle than claimed: The chain DEPTH penalty (+5/hop) still applies regardless of hop legitimacy. While Mailchimp won't trigger the "known redirector" penalty, a 3-hop chain (email→Mailchimp→landing) still incurs +5 NRS points from chain depth alone.

The gym fixture chain-04-legit-redirect.html explicitly documents that legitimate OAuth/UTM/login redirects "should NOT trigger redirect chain penalties" (lines 33, 35-36). However, the E2E test only covers a 2-hop scenario (within the depth threshold of 2), not a 3-hop scenario that would trigger the penalty.

The recommendation to use domain_groups.ts for organizational continuity is NOT implemented - domain_groups.ts exists but is not referenced in redirect_chain.ts or the chain scoring logic in nrs.ts.

Severity assessment: Medium is appropriate. +5 points alone unlikely to block (threshold 70) but could contribute to prompts in multi-factor attacks. The discrepancy between gym documentation (should NOT penalize legitimate chains) and actual implementation (still applies chain depth penalty) indicates this is a recognized gap.

findings.title: 3-D Secure payment redirect chains not handled; may prompt excessively
findings.evidence: No explicit handling for 3DS flows: checkout.com->issuer bank (e.g., secure3ds.bankofamerica.com)->merchant. This is 2-3 hop cross-site flow triggering nrs_cross_site (+20), nrs_redirect_chain_depth, possibly nrs_new_tab_window. No payment-specific domain recognition or redirect-pattern suppression in codebase.
findings.recommendation: Detect payment context: if source is e-commerce/checkout site (patterns: 'checkout', 'pay', 'cart', 'billing') and destination is known payment processor or issuing bank (Stripe, PayPal, Square, Visa, Mastercard, Amex, 3DS domains), suppress nrs_cross_site and redirect chain penalties. Store payment intent signal to suppress redirect-back-to-merchant as well.
findings.verdictNotes: The claim is confirmed by code analysis. NavSentinel applies nrs_cross_site (+20 points) unconditionally to cross-domain navigations (extension/src/shared/nrs.ts:92-95), including 3DS payment flows from checkout.com to issuing bank domains like secure3ds.bankofamerica.com. Checkout.com and issuing bank domains are not in the areSameOrganization() list (extension/src/shared/domain_groups.ts:23-71), so they are always treated as cross-site. Additionally, 3-hop redirect chains trigger nrs_redirect_chain_depth scoring (+5/hop, capped at +25) per extension/src/shared/redirect_chain.ts:132-137. No payment-specific suppression exists: payment processors (Stripe, PayPal, Square) and issuing banks are not recognized in DOMAIN_GROUPS, not allowlisted in redirect detection, and not exempted from cross-site penalties. In Smart mode (70 block threshold), a 2-hop 3DS flow scores ~30 NRS (prompts), and a 3-hop flow with redirector scores ~50 NRS (blocks in Strict mode). This creates legitimate user friction without explicit payment-context gating. The only relief is user allowlisting or the smart defaults mechanism (after 3 "Allow once" clicks). Severity assessment of "medium" is appropriate given the real-world impact on payment flows.

findings.title: SPA heavy DOM churn causes false-positive mutation alerts
findings.evidence: mutation_monitor.ts tracks overlay injection and form mutations. Benign scenario: Notion, Figma constantly inject toasts/tooltips (fixed, z-index>100). These trigger MutationAlert counts surfaced in debug output (capture_isolated.ts:205), potentially confusing users about risk. No per-domain allowlist for known SPAs/design tools.
findings.recommendation: Implement 'known SPA' domain list (Notion, Figma, Miro, Linear, Jira, Asana, Slack, Discord) and suppress alerts for these. Or use heuristic: classify small fixed overlays (z-index<1000, <2 sec duration, no forms/text) as 'ui_churn', exclude from alert count.
findings.verdictNotes: The core issue is real but details differ from claim: (1) The mutation_monitor.ts has NO domain-specific allowlist for Notion, Figma, Miro, Linear, Jira, Asana, Slack, Discord (confirmed at lines 60-110). (2) Benign overlays ARE partially handled via pattern matching - COOKIE_CONSENT_PATTERNS, CHAT_WIDGET_PATTERNS, and ARIA dialog role detection (lines 85-96, 101-110, 307-312). (3) CRITICAL: Low-severity overlays (cookie banners, chat widgets, ARIA dialogs) are downgraded from "high" to "low" severity and explicitly DO NOT trigger user-facing toasts - per capture_isolated.ts:982-984 comment: "Low-severity alerts (cookie banners, chat widgets, ARIA dialogs) are still logged for telemetry but do not disturb the user." Only HIGH-severity alerts show toast warnings (line 985). (4) The mutation monitor is intentionally delayed 2 seconds post-load to avoid flagging SPA hydration (mutation_monitor.ts:11). (5) Coverage threshold is MIN_OVERLAY_COVERAGE = 0.25 (25% of viewport), which filters small toasts. The FALSE-POSITIVE claim overstates UX impact - users don't actually see low-severity alerts as toasts. The ACTUAL gap is: no domain-based allowlist for known SPAs + reliance on class/id pattern matching means some small fixed overlays with z-index>=100 that don't match cookie/chat patterns could technically trigger alerts. But manifest impact is reduced: alerts are capped at 50/page, delayed 2 seconds, coverage-gated, and benign patterns are already downgraded. The recommendation (SPA domain allowlist or heuristic for small overlays) is reasonable but not addressing a severe user-facing false-positive flood - it's a refinement to suppress already-low-severity telemetry noise.

findings.title: Double-click frequency suppression missing for legitimate desktop-app-like interactions
findings.evidence: dblclick_guard.ts detects hijacking pattern (window.open + opener.location + rapid close). Benign scenario: Notion double-click to edit, Google Maps zoom, file managers. Current detection requires openerNavObserved flag but legitimate apps could open child window and have parent navigate concurrently without malice.
findings.recommendation: Add heuristics: (1) whitelist high-interaction sites (Notion, Figma, Google Maps, file managers); (2) suppress dblclick if child is same-origin (low-risk); (3) track user's dblclick pattern frequency per session and suppress if consistent with editing (same DOM region).
findings.verdictNotes: The core issue is real: dblclick detection lacks same-origin checks in the content-script layer (main_guard.ts:1170-1295 patchOpenerLocation, dblclick_guard.ts:118-127 isDoubleClickHijackActive). However, the claim's framing about openerNavObserved gating is incomplete—that flag only gates the Service Worker's child-close signal (sw.ts:903), not the main content-script detection. No whitelists for Notion/Figma/Google Maps exist (confirmed via repo search). No per-session frequency suppression exists either. The detection applies uniformly across all modes (capture_isolated.ts:1537-1592). Severity is mitigated somewhat by timing windows (DBLCLICK_WINDOW_MS=800ms, DBLCLICK_HIJACK_STALE_MS=5000ms in main_guard.ts:23,24) which limit FP surface to tight interaction windows, but the same-origin check recommendation is valid.

findings.title: Architecture: no session-aware state sharing between content script and service worker for FP suppression
findings.evidence: capture_isolated.ts (isolated-world content script) and sw.ts (service worker) have no reliable session-ephemeral state sharing. storage.session is per-frame-isolated; bridge_outbound.ts OutboundQueue drops messages under load; 'ns-allow-once' messages are fire-and-forget. No 'session context' object in decision pipeline means repeated prompts within minutes for same domain.
findings.recommendation: Introduce per-tab session-context store in service worker tracking 'recent_allows' (domain+timestamp) and 'recent_blocks'. Content scripts query via synchronous-style cached bridge call (<100ms block on first load, cached thereafter). Enables: (a) suppress prompts when user just allowed domain, (b) raise thresholds on benign traffic bursts, (c) lower on recent blocks. Current architecture has no feedback loop.
findings.verdictNotes:
The core architecture issue is CONFIRMED: there is no session-aware state sharing between content script (capture_isolated.ts) and service worker (sw.ts) for suppressing repeated prompts within minutes for the same domain. Key evidence:

1. allowUntilByTab (sw.ts:118) is per-tab and TTL-based (1.5s NAV_ALLOW_TTL_MS), NOT domain-pair based. It only survives across clicks on the SAME TAB, not across tabs or frames.

2. ns-allow-once (capture_isolated.ts:1228, main_guard.ts:761) is fire-and-forget with no response channel. It sets allowOnceRemaining=1 with 1200ms TTL in main_guard (line 180-182), but this is per-PAGE context, not shared with other frames/tabs.

3. No 'recent_allows' (domain+timestamp) map exists in the SW accessible to content scripts (session_state.ts lines 143-316 shows no such structure).

4. The decision pipeline (capture_isolated.ts:showAllowPrompt at line 1308) has NO check for recent domain-pair allows. It calls getPromptOutcomes() AFTER the decision (line 1325), only for adaptive scoring, not for prompt suppression.

5. bridge_outbound.ts (lines 45-65) confirms OutboundQueue drops messages under load, though ns-allow-once is marked PRIORITY_BRIDGE_TYPES (capture_isolated.ts:139).

However, the severity claim is PARTIALLY OVERSTATED: The 1.5-10s windows (allowUntilByTab, allowTargetByTab) DO suppress immediate re-prompts on same tab. Smart Defaults do track allowed domain pairs historically (smart_defaults.ts). The architecture is INTENTIONALLY per-tab (matching SW ephemeral nature). The claim correctly identifies the gap but doesn't acknowledge that per-tab suppression exists. The evidence file paths are accurate.

findings.title: No verbose audit mode for false-positive diagnosis
findings.evidence: Goal 2 (FRIEND-ADVISOR UX) requires 'every decision explainable in plain language via verbose mode / decision journal'. Current: debug_overlay.ts is developer opt-in (settings.debug flag); end users see only toast ('Suspicious new tab') or prompt. No persistent audit log of 'why was I prompted?' with full factor breakdown. popup/options UI lack 'recent decisions' or 'audit log' view.
findings.recommendation: Expose user-facing 'Decision Log' in options page showing last 50 nav/cred prompts/blocks with full factor breakdown: (a) NRS score+threshold, (b) all factors+weights, (c) domain_group/repeat-offender/adaptive adjustments applied, (d) user's choice+outcome. For benign FP: 'NRS was 45 (below 70) because: new_tab +20, cross_site +20, ua +5, no_history 0. Allowed.' Closes feedback loop, identifies systemic FP patterns.
findings.verdictNotes:
The claim is confirmed. Code review shows:

1. Debug overlay exists (extension/src/content/debug_overlay.ts) but is developer-only, gated by settings.debug flag (extension/src/options/options.ts:439, 468).

2. End users see only generic toast messages ("Suspicious new tab", "NavSentinel blocked a deceptive click") with buildPlainMessage() (extension/src/content/capture_isolated.ts:1710, 1733) that provides one explanation from reasonCodes.

3. PromptOutcomeEntry (extension/src/shared/storage.ts:55-64) stores only: id, ts, domain, destDomain, type, score, outcome, reasons (code strings only). Missing: NRS threshold used, all factor scores, CDS breakdown, adaptive adjustment amount, repeat-offender boost applied.

4. Options page Event Log (extension/src/options/options.ts:285-327) displays: event.kind, event.site, event.destHost, event.score, event.reasons.slice(0,4). No dedicated "Decision Log" tab, no factor/weight breakdown, no threshold comparison, no explanation of gating conditions.

5. Credential modal (extension/src/content/credential_guard.ts:154-162) shows risk score and getCredentialReasonLines() output (extension/src/content/credential_guard_model.ts:30-32), which returns only reason.label strings (up to 10), no factor scores or weights.

6. No user-facing UI exists for displaying:
   - Full factor breakdown with weights per decision
   - NRS score vs. NRS_BLOCK_THRESHOLD (70, or NRS_STRICT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD 50) comparison  
   - Domain repeat-offender boost (+10) or adaptive adjustments applied
   - Complete audit journal of recent prompts/blocks with reasoning
   - Systematic FP pattern identification

The absence of a "Decision Log" view in options.html (only generic "Event Log" at line 254) and the lack of structured decision metadata in PromptOutcomeEntry confirm the gap described in the claim.

findings.title: User activation adds only +5, insufficient for legitimate rapid-fire interactions
findings.evidence: nrs.ts:102-105: userActivationActive adds +5. Real scenario: user actively clicking in web app, legitimate link opens in new tab; NRS=45 (0 CDS + 20 new-tab + 20 cross-site + 5 UA) still prompts (threshold=70). User proved intent by clicking but +5 insufficient to offset structural penalty.
findings.recommendation: If userActivationActive=true AND visible/named anchor: suppress nrs_new_tab_window (set to 0 instead of +20) OR reduce threshold by 10. Or add 'active_engagement' factor worth -15 when both UA active and visible anchor true, offsetting new-tab penalty.

findings.title: No adaptive thresholds for common corporate domain patterns
findings.evidence: adaptive_scoring.ts adjusts ±15 based on user behavior, but only after events accumulate. First visit to corporate tool (herokuapp/vercel/netlify) has no special handling: adaptiveAdjustment=0 (capture_isolated.ts:124). Real scenario: employee at new job accessing internal tool on herokuapp.com; every click to okta.com prompts because domain has no history.
findings.recommendation: Add lightweight heuristic for 'likely-corporate' patterns: if source contains 'internal', 'staging', 'dev', 'corp', '.herokuapp.com', '.vercel.app', '.netlify.app', apply -10 threshold adjustment (70->60) on first visit. Not a trust list (user can block), but recognition that these environments have normal cross-site auth nav.

findings.title: Credential guard does not leverage navigation's session-based allow pattern
findings.evidence: credential_guard.ts and credential_guard_model.ts prompt independently from navigation Smart Mode. User allowing nav to okta.com may still prompt on form-submit to same okta domain. This is intentional (credentials stricter) but creates friction. No cross-seam memory between guards (credential_guard_model.ts shouldPrompt() doesn't check recent nav allows).
findings.recommendation: Implement cross-seam memory: if navigation to domain D allowed <=1 min ago, suppress credential guard's medium-risk prompt when D appears as form-action. Retains strict cold-visit checking while reducing friction on hot sessions.

findings.title: Firefox compat: storage.session fallback not cleared on reload; session-aware suppression compromised
findings.evidence: browser.ts:82-112: Firefox lacks storage.session; fallback uses storage.local with SESSION_PREFIX. Fallback is NOT auto-cleared on reload (only on unload). Session-based suppression (e.g., 'allow okta for this session') will persist across navigations, reducing security.
findings.recommendation: Use TTL-based session suppression instead: store recent-allows with timestamps, check if (now-allowedAt<60000). More portable, works on Chrome+Firefox. Or document trade-off and accept session-suppression is Chrome-only.

findings.title: Service worker restart loses domain_profile repeat-offender context
findings.evidence: domain_profile.ts stores to chrome.storage.local (persistent), but in-memory map lost on SW restart. Fresh load re-reads from storage; getDomainRisk() re-reads on each call, but context temporarily lost between restart and first nav. Not critical (domain_profile is tie-breaker), but affects user experience on SW crash.
findings.recommendation: Document as acceptable or implement lightweight 'domain bloom filter' of repeat offenders bundled at build-time from prior session, so fresh SW has context for most-flagged domains.

findings.title: Silent allow decisions emit zero events—user cannot discover why a click was allowed or what was evaluated
findings.evidence: extension/src/content/capture_isolated.ts:1676-1756 implements core nav decision logic. When decision='allow' (line 1744), the code sends icon update, posts to main, notifies nav gesture, but does NOT call appendEventSafely() or appendOutcomeSafely(). Events are logged ONLY for prompt (nav_blank_prompt line 1363) and block (nav_click_block line 1718). Result: (1) a click scored NRS=35 (safe) produces zero event, (2) user never sees the evaluation, (3) popup gauge (popup.ts:199) stays at 0/green for domains that only get silent allows, creating false reassurance that domain is pristine when it was evaluated 20 times. The popup can only show risk from SCORED events (events with score field), and silent allows have no score recorded.
findings.recommendation: Emit 'nav_allow_silent' event for every silent allow: appendEventSafely({ kind: 'nav_allow_silent', site: siteKeyFromLocation(), url: location.href, destHost: parsed?.host ?? null, score: nrs, reasons: reasonCodes, extra: { cds, nrsFactors, adaptiveAdjustment, blockThreshold, decision: 'allow' } }) at line 1744. findings.title: Chrome MV3 Cannot Block Navigation Before Commit—Only Reactive Rollback (User-Visible Flash).
findings.evidence: manifest.json declares declarativeNetRequest (lines 14, 65-73); extension/rules/dnr_static.json (lines 1-22) contains placeholder rules. However, DNR rules are static per MV3 spec—cannot be dynamically computed per-click context. webRequest with blocking is not available in Chrome MV3 (only Firefox MV2). The extension's only real mitigation is rollback (main_guard.ts ~line 400, ns-rollback message): allow nav to commit, then execute history.back(). User sees a visible flash of the attacker domain before rollback completes. This contradicts goal vision #1: 'ZERO false positives in everyday Smart Mode browsing — the extension must be silent during normal use...yet still catch real attacks.' Rollback is *not* silent; it is user-visible.
findings.recommendation: This is a Chrome MV3 structural limit; no pure-software solution exists. Three escape hatches: (a) **Firefox MV2 native build** (issue #173/FF-01 merged; FF-02/FF-03/FF-04 stacked, blocked on AI-4 tooling decision): Firefox MV2 has webRequest.onBeforeRequest with 'cancel' action, enabling true proactive blocking before commit. Cost: 1-2 weeks after AI-4 decision; value: proactive blocking, silent operation on Firefox, product differentiation. (b) **Native-messaging companion process** (not yet scoped in roadmap): persistent process intercepts DNS or network egress before browser opens the socket, preventing any visual flash. Cost: high (C/C++/Rust native component, cross-platform); value: highest—works on both Chrome and Firefox. (c) **Accept rollback for Chrome; optimize UX**: minimize flash delay in history.back() call (~100-300ms currently); inject a frame-blocking overlay immediately on risky-nav detection (before commit) so user sees 'NavSentinel blocked this navigation' instead of the attacker domain; add collapsible factor breakdown toast. This trades silent→transparent but eliminates confusion.
findings.verdictNotes: The claim conflates two separate mechanisms. CONFIRMED: Chrome MV3 does NOT have webRequest.onBeforeRequest with blocking capability (line 14 in manifest.json shows only declarativeNetRequest, not webRequest). Rollback exists and can cause visual flash. REFUTED: The claim wrongly asserts that rollback is NavSentinel's "only real mitigation" and that the extension cannot prevent navigation before commit. The actual architecture uses PROACTIVE JavaScript API patching as the primary defense: patchedOpen() (main_guard.ts:499-539) prevents window.open from executing immediately by returning null and storing the action; patchedAssign/patchedReplace (lines 551-639) similarly block location navigation; patchedFormSubmit (lines 641-699) blocks form submission—all returning immediately without executing the risky action. These are fully executed client-side BEFORE navigation commit. The blocked actions are stored in blockedActions map (line 140) and only executed when explicitly allowed via isolated-world messages (lines 781-790). In Smart Mode (mode === "smart", line 107), popup intent allowances prevent false positives on legitimate popups (lines 272-285). The secondary reactive rollback (onCommittedHandler in sw.ts:712) only triggers when a top-frame navigation COMMITS despite these guards—e.g., user-typed URL or redirect chains. Smart Mode silent operation is mostly achieved for JS-initiated attacks (the primary threat). The claim's severity is OVERSTATED: it characterizes the entire system as reactive rollback when it is actually proactive API blocking with rollback as a secondary fallback for top-frame commit scenarios.

findings.title: Main<->Isolated Bridge Has No Liveness Check or Heartbeat—Dead Port Silences All Signals Until Next Nav.
findings.evidence: extension/src/content/main_guard.ts (lines 34-44) defines bridge state: bridgePort, bridgeSession, bridgeVerified, bridgeChallenge. failBridgeHandshake() (lines 93-105) tears down incomplete handshakes after BRIDGE_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS (3s, line 19). However, once the bridge is verified (bridgeVerified = true), there is NO heartbeat or liveness monitor. If the isolated world crashes (rare, but possible under memory pressure) or the port is closed by page script, the MAIN guard's postToIsolated() (lines 45-60) will continue to call bridgePort.postMessage() on a dead port, and the message will silently fail without retry or error callback. The port's messageerror event is never wired. Impact: if isolated world crashes, the MAIN guard keeps firing blocked-action signals into the void (pendingOutbound is drained and messages sent over dead port); user sees no feedback; prompt outcomes and decisions not recorded.
findings.recommendation: Add ns-ping ↔ ns-pong heartbeat: (a) MAIN guard sends ns-ping every 5 seconds while bridgeVerified=true. (b) Isolated world responds with ns-pong. (c) If MAIN guard receives 2 consecutive missed pongs (10s window), set bridgeVerified=false and fall back to buffering outbound messages in pendingOutbound queue. (d) On next user gesture or navigation, attempt re-handshake via the existing challenge-response protocol. Also add a messageerror listener to the port (bridgePort.onmessageerror = ...) to detect port closure and immediately trigger re-handshake. This prevents silent message loss and keeps the user informed of bridge failures via the debug log (postToIsolated('ns-bridge-error', {reason: '...'})). Effort: **M** (1-2 hours, isolated to main_guard.ts + capture_isolated.ts bridge handler).
findings.verdictNotes: The core technical vulnerability is confirmed: once bridgeVerified=true (line 36, 901), there is NO mechanism to detect if the port dies. If the isolated world crashes after verification, postToIsolated() (lines 45-60) will call postMessage() on a dead port with no error handling (no onmessageerror listener exists anywhere). However, the claim's severity framing has a mitigation: (1) the ping/pong check (lines 756-758 main_guard.ts) is a one-time check during initialization, not periodic as claimed. (2) failBridgeHandshake() (lines 93-105) only applies during the 3s handshake window (line 923), not after verification. The claim is correct that there's no POST-VERIFICATION liveness check, but it overstates the ping/pong as a countermeasure—it only applies pre-verification. The actual gap is: once verification succeeds, if the port becomes dead before the next navigation, messages will silently fail until navigation triggers a new handshake attempt. The vulnerability is real but somewhat mitigated by the fact that handshake re-establishment attempts do occur on new message init events (lines 855-926), though users would see no feedback during that gap. In Smart Mode, this affects blocked-action recording and decision relay (ns-allow/ns-allow-action messages) since those use the same bridge.

findings.title: Chrome MV3 Platform Limit: CSP Header Blindness—Content Scripts Cannot See HTTP Response Headers.
findings.evidence: extension/src/content/csp_analyzer.ts (lines 9-10, 24-29) explicitly documents: 'Content scripts in the isolated world can read meta tags but cannot see HTTP response headers, so only meta-tag CSP is checked.' Because meta-tag CSP is attacker-controlled (line 11-14), CSP is only used as a risk-*elevating* modifier (weakness scoring), never as a safety signal. Two residual risks: (1) **false positives on strict-header CSP sites**: a legitimate site with strong HTTP Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' header will appear weak to NavSentinel if the site lacks or has a weak meta-tag CSP, causing spurious score elevation. (2) **false negatives on fake meta-tag CSP**: an attacker serving a page with a fake nonce-based meta-tag CSP cannot bypass NavSentinel's phishing detection, but the fake CSP itself is useless as a safety signal. Issue #179 is tracked but remains open.
findings.recommendation: No solution in pure Chrome MV3. Three escape hatches: (a) **Firefox MV2 with webRequest.onHeadersReceived**: can inspect actual HTTP headers before content-script stage, enabling real CSP scoring. Cost: tied to Firefox port (AI-4 decision). Value: eliminates false positives on strict-header sites. (b) **Native-messaging companion**: proxy HTTP traffic and inspect headers server-side. Cost: high. (c) **Workaround for Chrome**: document the limitation in help text: 'NavSentinel can only read CSP meta-tags, not HTTP headers. If you see many false positives on a trusted site with a strict Content-Security-Policy header, please manually allowlist the domain.' Add a debug-log entry when CSP is detected via meta-tag only, noting that the signal is attacker-controlled and low-confidence. Prioritize issue #179 after AI-4 (Firefox tooling decision)—if Firefox MV2 is chosen, unlocking header inspection becomes a medium-effort follow-up.
findings.verdictNotes: The core architectural claim is correct: Chrome MV3 content scripts cannot access HTTP response headers, so NavSentinel only reads meta-tag CSP. The code in extension/src/content/csp_analyzer.ts (lines 8-14) explicitly documents this and confirms meta-tag CSP is attacker-controlled and only used for risk elevation, never reduction. However, the severity is overstated. The actual implementation (nrs.ts lines 181-184) applies CSP weakness only when nrs > 20, meaning the false positive scenario only manifests on navigations that already have significant risk factors (new tab, cross-site, clickfix, etc.). A legitimate site with strong HTTP CSP but no meta-tag CSP won't trigger false positives in Smart Mode unless the user action is already suspicious (base NRS > 20). Additionally, issue #179 is formally tracked (ORCHESTRATOR.md, commit a3bd12d) but classified as LOW severity ("MV3 limitation"), not HIGH. The residual risks and escape hatches described are accurate. The main inaccuracy is framing this as a high-severity detection flaw when it's a gated modifier that only amplifies already-detected risk signals.

findings.title: Firefox MV3 Session Storage Fallback Not Auto-Cleared on Restart—Stale Tab State Persists Silently.
findings.evidence: extension/src/shared/browser.ts (lines 85-167) implements storageSessionShim: when chrome.storage.session is absent (Firefox MV3), it falls back to storage.local with 'ns_session:' prefix (line 68, SESSION_PREFIX). The comment on line 162 explicitly states: 'The fallback is NOT auto-cleared on browser restart the way real session storage is; FF-03 (session_state compat) tracks closing that semantic gap.' This means a Firefox user who restarts their browser will retain stale tab state from *before* the restart (allowUntilByTab, gestureUntilByTab, typedOriginByTab, etc., defined in session_state.ts lines 145-167). The SessionStateManager.hydrate() call on SW startup (line 183) will restore these stale entries from the fallback storage without any version check or warning. User impact: (1) a navigation allowance granted before restart will linger as a spurious allow even though the browser session is fresh; (2) tab-id reuse across restarts could cause old tab-1's state to be incorrectly correlated with new tab-1; (3) there is no debug-log entry or UI indicator signaling that the session store is fallback-based and not auto-cleared. This is tracked as issue FF-03 but deferred pending FF-02 (Vite build config decision AI-4).
findings.recommendation: For Firefox MV3 (FF-03, stacked on FF-02): (a) Add a version field to the session store (ns_session_version: 1) set by SW on first startup. On subsequent hydrate() calls, check whether the version is missing or stale (e.g., version is from 2+ hours ago, implying a browser restart). If stale, ignore the fallback storage entirely and rebuild session state from scratch. (b) Wire the debug overlay or options diagnostic panel to display 'Session storage: native (Chrome)' or 'Session storage: fallback (Firefox)—last hydrated at HH:MM, restarted cache cleared' so users see the state clearly. (c) In options page, add a diagnostic panel showing current session entry counts (captureTimestampsByTab.size, oauthFlowByTab.size, etc.) and the last hydration timestamp. This removes the silent stale-state risk and surfaces Firefox-specific limitations to users. Effort: **M** (3-4 hours, touches session_state.ts, browser.ts, options.ts). Blocks: FF-02 tooling decision (AI-4).
findings.verdictNotes:
ANALYSIS: The claimed issue is UNVERIFIABLE in current code because Firefox MV3 support (FF-02/FF-03) has NOT been implemented. The roadmap states FF-02 is pending a tooling decision (AI-4), FF-03 is stacked on FF-02, and neither has begun.

EVIDENCE OF CURRENT STATE:
1. `vite.config.ts` only builds Chrome version (line 4: `import manifest from "./extension/manifest.json"`)
2. `manifest.firefox.json` exists but references non-existent `src/sw/background.html` (which FF-02 is supposed to create)
3. Firefox build is not active in any build script

CRITICAL CODE FLAW (if Firefox support is ever implemented):
The claim correctly identifies that the fallback mechanism has a fundamental architectural flaw. Line 191 in `extension/src/shared/session_state.ts` shows `_doHydrate()` calls `chrome.storage.session.get()` directly, NOT the `storageSessionShim` defined in `extension/src/shared/browser.ts` (lines 165-167). The shim is exported but NEVER USED - persist operations also hardcode `chrome.storage.session` (lines 224, 232, 259).

This means:
- If FF-03 implements Firefox support without fixing this, the hydrate logic would crash on line 191 because `chrome.storage.session` is undefined on Firefox
- The correct approach would be to inject/use `storageSessionShim` throughout session_state.ts, but currently only `browser.ts` has the shim logic
- There is NO version check, restart detection, or clear-on-restart logic in the current code (claim's point is valid)

SEVERITY CORRECTION:
The claim rates this as "high" but should note it's currently theoretical (Firefox support undeployed). The architectural flaw exists and WOULD manifest when FF-03 is implemented IF not fixed first.

FILE PATHS:
- `extension/src/shared/session_state.ts:191` - hardcoded `chrome.storage.session`
- `extension/src/shared/browser.ts:165-167` - unused `storageSessionShim` export
- `vite.config.ts:4` - Chrome-only build

findings.title: Visual-Sim Spoof Detection Plumbing Complete but Inert—Placeholder Hashes Never Fire True Positives.
findings.evidence: extension/src/content/visual_sim_capture.ts (lines 51-100+) is fully implemented: captures viewport via SW message, downsamples to 8x8 (aHash) and 16x16 (bHash), compares against template database using confirmBHashMatch(). extension/src/shared/visual_sim_templates.ts loads brand_templates.json and provides findAHashCandidates() and computeVisualSimScore(). However, scripts/build-brand-templates.mjs generates placeholder template hashes using seeded Math.random() instead of real brand login pages. The ACTION_ITEMS.md note on AI-5 confirms: 'ships PLACEHOLDER template hashes...so it can never fire a true positive. Replacing them needs hashes built from real brand login pages—sourcing/sanctioning those screenshots is a product/legal call only you can make.' The plumbing is production-ready and fully tested; the detection is architecturally inert. Tracked as AI-5, waiting for user decision.
findings.recommendation: This is a **product/legal decision, not a technical gap**: (1) Source (or point to) sanctioned login screenshots for at least 20 major brands (PayPal, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Apple, Adobe, Salesforce, etc.). (2) Run real screenshots through scripts/build-brand-templates.mjs to generate actual aHash and bHash values. (3) Replace the placeholder entries in extension/public/brand_templates.json with the real hashes. (4) Ship the updated extension. Once real hashes exist, visual-sim detection automatically fires on matched pages—no code changes required. The blocker is (a) sourcing high-quality screenshots from each brand's real login page, (b) confirming legal/trademark sign-off to use them in detection hashing (brand-association liability). Decision point tracked as AI-5 in ACTION_ITEMS.md, awaiting user confirmation. Effort (once decision made): **S** (< 4 hours, script + config file update).
findings.verdictNotes:
The visual-similarity spoof detection plumbing is production-ready and fully integrated, but will never fire true positives because the templates use placeholder hashes that don't correspond to real brand login pages.

CONFIRMED FACTS:
1. Pipeline implementation (extension/src/content/visual_sim_capture.ts lines 51-139): Fully implemented - captures viewport via SW message (line 74), downsamples to 8x8 for aHash (line 84) and 16x16 for bHash (line 97), calls confirmBHashMatch() (line 103).

2. Placeholder template hashes (scripts/build-brand-templates.mjs lines 88-101): Uses deterministic SHA-256 hashing on brand IDs, not real perceptual hashes from actual screenshots. Example: generateAHash uses 'sha256:google:v1' → first 8 bytes. These hashes are stored in extension/public/brand_templates.json with generated date 2026-05-16.

3. Likelihood of matching real pages: Zero. Real brand login pages would have completely different perceptual hashes (computed from actual pixels). The placeholder hashes are cryptographic derivatives with no correlation to actual page appearance. The hamming distance thresholds (aHash ≤ 10, bHash ≤ 25, extension/src/shared/visual_sim_types.ts lines 43-44) will never be met by chance.

4. Integration into NRS decision-making (extension/src/content/capture_isolated.ts lines 1614, 1650): visualSimilarityScore is retrieved via getVisualSimScoreForNRS() and passed to computeNRS() in the NavigationContext. Line 1650 only includes non-zero scores. In nrs.ts lines 201-204, when visualSimilarityScore > 0, it adds up to NRS_WEIGHT_VISUAL_SIM_CAP (30 points).

5. Mode gating: Visual-sim check runs when settings.defaultMode !== "off" (lines 274, 872, 900). This means it executes in BOTH smart and strict modes, not just smart mode.

6. ACTION_ITEMS.md AI-5 confirmation: Lines 116-123 explicitly state the detection is "architecturally inert" until real brand login screenshots are sourced, described as a "product/legal decision."

INACCURACIES IN THE CLAIM:
- The claim states "seeded Math.random()" but the actual implementation uses deterministic SHA-256, not any PRNG. The comment in build-brand-templates.mjs line 8 incorrectly calls it "seeded PRNG" but the code clearly uses createHash('sha256').
- The claim says the detection fires based on "Smart Mode" but the code gates on `defaultMode !== "off"`, meaning it runs in both smart AND strict modes (lines 274, 872, 900, 915, etc. all check !== "off", not === "smart").

The core detection gap is REAL and verified: the hashes are placeholders and will never match real pages, making the entire pipeline inert from a detection perspective.
